This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed by appellants/claimants, challenging the impugned award dated 25.11.2014 passed by12th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No.109/2014.

entities.text: by12th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. A few facts necessary for the adjudication of this appeal, as narrated, are that on 12.04.2012 at around 7:30 AM, deceased, Dinesh Singh Gaur, was traveling from Bhopal to Gwalior with his son and others in a car bearing registration no. MP33-1970.

Deceased Dinesh Singh Gaur was driving the car slowly and cautiously on his side of the road when he reached near Gandhi Dargah turn, AB Road at that time, a truck bearing registration no. UP80-BM-9619, driven by Brajesh Thakur, was being driven rashly and negligently.

The truck dashed into the deceased's car, resulting in grievous NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:535 2 MA-616-2015 injuries to Dinesh Singh Gaur,
who later succumbed to his injuries during treatment.
A First Information Report (FIR) was lodged at Police Station Narshing Garh, District Rajgarh vide Crime No. 126/2012 under Section 304-A of IPC against the driver of the truck.
After the investigation, a charge sheet was filed before the competent Court against the driver- Brajesh Thakur.
The claim petition was subsequently filed before the Claims Tribunal.

The Tribunal, in its impugned award, held 25% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and awarded a compensation of Rs.33,06,736/- with an interest rate of 7.5% per annum in favor of claimants.

Following the passing of the award, the Insurance Company Smt.Manju Gaur vs Sanjiv Parmar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61829125/
1 filed MCC No.16 of 2014 before the Claims Tribunal for recalculation of award.

entities.text: Insurance Company Smt.Manju Gaur vs Sanjiv Parmar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 18.02.2015, the Tribunal reduced the compensation amount to Rs.29,53,776/- The claimants, being dissatisfied with the same, have filed the present Miscellaneous Appeal, seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. It is contended on behalf of appellants that learned Claims Tribunal erred in appreciating the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court and in awarding a compensation that is on the lower side.
The Claims Tribunal deducted 10% income tax from the deceased's total yearly income of Rs.3,83,304/-.After proper deductions, the annual income of deceased should be considered as Rs.
. Considering the deceased's bright future, 50% future prospects should be added to the yearly income.
This would bring the yearly income to Rs.5,47,956/-.
After deducting 1/3rd for personal expenses, the claimants have argued that the yearly dependency should be Rs.3,65,304/-.

A multiplier of 13 should be applied based on the age of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:535 3 MA-616-2015 deceased, which would result in a compensation of Rs.47,48,952/-.
The claimants contended that the amounts awarded for funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of companionship, etc., are too low and should be enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/-.
The claimants argued that there was no substantial evidence to show that deceased was contributory negligent.
The truck driver Brajesh Thakur is solely responsible for the alleged accident.

In support of contentions, appellants have placed reliance on the decisions of Syed Sadiq etc. vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company (2014 ACJ 627), National Insurance Company vs. Smt. Mithlesh and Others (Misc. Appeal No. 155 of 2017,
dated 25th September 2023) Shankarlal and Another vs. Duli and Others (Misc. Appeal No. 456 of 2011, dated 30th November 2022).

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company opposeed the claimants' contentions and has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bijoy Kumar Dugar vs. Bidyadhar Dutta and Others (2006 (1) TAC 969 SC), wherein it was held that in a head- on collision, both drivers should be held equally responsible.

entities.text: Bijoy Kumar Dugar vs. Bidyadhar Dutta and Others (2006 (1) TAC 969 SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for Insurance Company further cited the decision in Kamini and Others vs. KP Sharma and Others (2009 (2) TAC 397) , which states that when the spot map showing the position of the vehicles at the time of the accident is not produced, it is reasonable to assume that the deceased contributed 25% to the accident in case of a head-on collision.
5. Heard learned Counsel for the parties.

entities.text: Kamini and Others vs. KP Sharma and Others (2009 (2) TAC 397)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In the case of Smt. Mithlesh (supra), the Coordinate Bench of this NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:535 4 MA-616-2015 Court has held as under:-
''15.

Claimants have examined Mithlesh, wife of the deceased, as AW-1 who has proved documents which are part of the charge- sheet filed against the driver of the offending vehicle in respect to this accident as per Ex.P-5 to P-13.
Claimants have also examined eye-witnesses Satendra Singh and Mahendra as AW-3 and AW-4 respectively.

AW-1 Mithlesh admitted that she was not present on the place of occurrence at the time of accident, however, on the basis of her evidence, it is proved Smt.Manju Gaur vs Sanjiv Parmar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61829125/
2 that a criminal case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle and after investigation, charge-sheet was filed under Section 304-A of IPC on account of death of Raghvendra in this accident.

entities.text: Smt.Manju Gaur vs Sanjiv Parmar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Driver of the offending vehicle did not appear to contradict the details of accident as narrated by the eye-witnesses examined by the claimants.

Learned claims tribunal only on account of spot map held that the accident was the result of contributory negligence of the deceased, however, the eye-witnesses examined by the claimants has denied the fact that deceased was negligent at the time of accident.

Eye-witness Mahendra (AW-4 ) in his cross- examination at para 7 has specifically stated that there are two different roads one from Gwalior to Bhind and another from Bhind to Gwalior having a divider between the roads, however, he has clearly stated that there was no divider on the gate of the colony and people cross the road on the place where divider is not built.

16. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sayed Sadiq and others Vs.Divisional Manager,
United India Insurance Company ltd.;
2014 ACJ627 held that "if the contribution of the deceased in the accident is not proved by the respondents by producing evidence, the findings of the Tribunal regarding contributory negligence cannot be upheld".
17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court in the case of Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kauvargi Tak and others; SLP (Civil) No.5436/1994, held that : "It is important to note that the respondents did not contend before the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the appellant, the driver of the car.

entities.text: Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kauvargi Tak and others; SLP (Civil) No.5436/1994
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There was not even an allegation in the written statement filed by the respondents that the car driver was negligent and the accident occurred as result of partial negligence of the car driver.
In this factual situation, it cannot be held that there was contributory negligence on the part of the deceased".

18. The Apex Court in the case of Shanker Singh Vs. Mahesh; MACD 2013(1) MP 262, held that : "So far as the contributory negligence on the part of the appellant is concerned, since criminal case was registered against the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.1 did not turn up to explain in what circumstances accident occurred, this court is of the view that the learned tribunal was not justified in holding the appellant liable for accident, the finding of contributory negligence stands set aside".
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:535 5 MA-616-2015 7.

entities.text: Shanker Singh Vs. Mahesh; MACD 2013(1) MP 262
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On perusal of record of Claims Tribunal, it is found that the Claims Tribunal had assigned 25%
contributory negligence to the deceased based on the absence of a spot map.
However, contributory negligence must be established with cogent and substantial evidence.
In the absence of a spot map and eyewitness testimony, the finding of contributory negligence is speculative and cannot be sustained.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal is set aside.

8. Upon perusal of the record, it is found that deceased's wife, Mrs. Manju (AW1), testified that her husband was serving as an Executive Engineer (EE) in the MP Housing Board, earning a monthly Smt.Manju Gaur vs Sanjiv Parmar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61829125/
3 salary of Rs.33,000/-.
However, deceased's son, Raviraj (AW2), stated that his father's monthly salary was Rs.31,934/-.

Furthermore, Lakshmi Shivhare (AW3), a divisional accountant with the Housing Board, produced deceased's last full salary certificate (Exhibit P-14), which indicated a salary of Rs.32,934/- for the final month of service.

She clarified in her cross- examination that this salary certificate did not reflect deductions for income tax and professional tax, as these deductions are made up to February, and salary certificate pertains to March.
According to her statement, after applying the applicable deductions, net salary of deceased was Rs. 31,104/- per month.

Additionally,
Raviraj (AW2) produced key documents including the service book of deceased (Exhibit P-13), his posting letter in the MP Housing Board (Exhibits P-14 and P-15), and a salary certificate (Exhibit P- 16).
Mrs. Manju (AW1) also submitted original certificates received by her husband from Election Commission (Exhibits P-11 and P-12).

These NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:535 6 MA-616-2015 documents confirms that deceased, Dinesh Singh, had been appointed as Project Engineer (Assistant Engineer) in the Building Construction Art Centre, Ratlam, on 14.01.1992, and was regularized in this position on 02.10.1992.
Subsequently, he was posted to MP Housing Board on 20.08.2010.
The service book of deceased further records his deputation to the Housing and Infrastructure Development Board Zone-1, Bhopal, and his death on 01.02.2012.

entities.text: Housing and Infrastructure Development Board Zone-1,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
On going through the aforesaid evidence, including the salary certificates, service records, and supporting testimonies,
this Court agrees with claimants' arguments regarding appropriate income tax deduction and inclusion of future prospects.
Consequently, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation amount as outlined below:-

Particulars   Monthly Income of Deceased 31  Annual Income (31934  12) 3,
 Taxable Income (3,83,208 - 1,60,000) 2,
Income After 10% Tax Deduction (2,00,887= 2,23,208-10% + 3,60,887 1,60,000) Income After Deducting Professional Tax (3, 60,887 - 2,500) 3,58,387 Future Prospects (30% )= 4,65,903 (3,58,387+1,07,516) Dependency (2/3rd x 4,65,903) 3,10,602
Multiplier (Age of Deceased: 13)

40,37,826/-
40,000x3 + 30,0000= Other Heads (consortium, Funeral, Loss of Estate, etc.) 1,50,000 Total Compensation 41,87,826/ Amount Already Awarded by Tribunal 29,53,776 Enhancement of Compensation 12,23,050 9

Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.
41,87,826/- as against the amount of Rs.29,53,776/- awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.12,23,050/-.

The NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:535 7 MA-616-2015 enhanced compensation will carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the claimants within three months from the date of receipt of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the claimants shall deposit the differential Court fee, if not already paid, within a period of one month and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue a certified copy of this order.
